title: fastpath: improve fallback gating + precision toggle safe-mode for KV/continuous batching
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: The fastpath gives large throughput and latency wins for the common case, but we've seen intermittent correctness skews when precision toggles or KV-cache state diverge across execution paths. This PR tightens fastpath gating and introduces a deterministic 'safe-mode' for precision toggles + KV cache to guarantee correctness while retaining most perf benefits.

Summary of changes (commits merged):
- Introduce runtime flag prefer_fastpath + fine-grained gating logic in scheduler (commit: add-fastpath-gating).
- Add precision_fuse toggle and safe-mode validators that force deterministic fallback when mixed-precision hazards are detected (commit: precision-safe-mode).
- Harden KV cache handling: validate serialized KV headers and fall back to slowpath on mismatch, plus unit tests (commit: kv-safe-mode-tests).
- Improve continuous batching interactions: ensure batch composition respects fastpath constraints (commit: batching-fastpath-compat).
- Add perf benchmarks and telemetry for fastpath fallbacks (commit: perf/telemetry-fastpath).

What changed (high level):
- Scheduler now evaluates a small predicate before dispatching to the fastpath; fastpath is allowed only when: (a) requested precision profile matches cached compiled kernels, (b) KV cache header checksum matches runtime expectations, and (c) request-level override flags don't opt out. Otherwise scheduler routes to the verified slowpath.
- precision_fuse enables a quantization/precision-safety check at model load + first inference. If a mismatch is detected, the node enters safe-mode: subsequent requests use slowpath until an explicit recompile/flush.
- KV cache changes add a compact header fingerprint and validation step. On detection of a mismatch (e.g. cache from model variant or different quantization), runtime invalidates cache or routes request to slowpath instead of attempting speculative merges.
- Telemetry: new metrics fastpath.dispatch_attempts, fastpath.fallback_reasons (labels: precision_mismatch, kv_checksum, override), and fastpath.fallback_rate. These are emitted at decision time and can be used to drive canary thresholds.

Tests & CI:
- Added unit tests for KV safe-mode and precision_fuse (tests/unit/test_kv_safe_mode.cc).
- Added integration perf bench that reproduces prior regression locally (tests/perf/bench_fastpath_batching.py).
- CI: initial run had a flaky test due to timing in batching; fixed by introducing a deterministic scheduling seed. Final CI state: pass.

Performance impact:
- Microbenchmarks (seq_len=16, batch_size=32) show median throughput +18-25% on A100 when prefer_fastpath is true and fastpath constraints satisfied.
- Telemetry shows ~4% fallback rate in mixed precision workloads during a 24h internal canary. Fallbacks reduce throughput to slowpath baseline but preserve correctness.

Compatibility & rollout plan:
- Default behavior: prefer_fastpath=true, precision_fuse=false (backwards compatible). Operators can enable precision_fuse to opt-in to strict safety gating.
- Canary rollout performed on a 5% fleet with telemetry gating; observed expected fallback patterns and no correctness regressions reported.
- Docs updated with runbook and rollback steps (docs/operational/runbooks/fastpath-fallback.md).

Notes on tradeoffs:
- This PR chooses correctness over speculative perf: when in doubt the scheduler prefers slowpath. The precision_fuse opt-in allows teams to be stricter. Future work includes pre-warming fastpath-compatible kernels and async KV cache validation to reduce fallback rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Add gating predicate and flags
- [x] Add KV header fingerprint + tests
- [x] Add telemetry for fallbacks
- [x] Add perf benchmarks and iterate on flaky test
- [x] Update docs and runbooks

CI/Checks:
- Build: passed
- Unit tests: passed
- Perf benchmarks (CI smoke): passed
- Lint: passed

Merge: Squash-merge after reviewer approvals and green CI.
